summary: Reviewed the five-file change against the base commit, including MkDocs 1.6.1 pathspec/exclusion behavior, the i18n plugin file tree, documentation link checks, and the new Magpie reviewer-selection instructions. The site exclusion for `docs/AGENTS.md` is effective and leaves no AGENTS page in the loaded file set; the main concrete defect is that the new Magpie command recipe does not yield the systems-file values it claims, because `magpie <agent> model` returns a human-readable label rather than the bare model id.

findings.title: Magpie field output is transcribed as model id, breaking reviewer invocation
findings.trigger: An agent follows the documented sequence with the installed Magpie: runs `magpie codex model`, gets `Codex model ctrip-ada/claude-auto[1M]`, then writes that returned string verbatim as `model` in the systems file.
findings.consequence: The benchmark adapter passes that whole sentence to `codex exec --model`, so the reviewer either fails to start or is attributed to a nonexistent model instead of CTrip ADA's `ctrip-ada/claude-auto[1M]`; per-run provenance is wrong and the review cannot run as instructed.
findings.evidence: `.agents/skills/multi-review/SKILL.md:53-56` instructs querying `magpie <agent> model` and writing the returned model/provider into the systems file. The installed command prints a labeled sentence (`Codex model ctrip-ada/claude-auto[1M]`) rather than a bare id. `tools/llm-review-bench/src/protocol/config.ts:61-77` accepts the value as `model` unchanged, and `tools/llm-review-bench/src/adapters/codex.ts:32-35` forwards it unchanged via `args.push('--model', system.model)`.
findings.suggestedFix: Document a machine-readable extraction or supported field output that returns the bare model slug, or explicitly require stripping the `Codex model ` / agent label and splitting only the actual `provider/model` slug before writing it to the systems file; add the exact command and expected output to the skill.
